meta.title: Pricing
meta.description: Pay-as-you-go model prices: input, output, cache and image prices for all three channels on one page.

hero.title: One transparent price list
hero.subtitle: Pay as you go with no subscriptions or monthly fees. What you see is exactly what the selected channel is billed.

tables.unitCny: Prices in CNY at $1 = ¥{rate}; wallets are charged in USD
tables.imageUnit: Per image or per 1M output tokens

notes.title: Billing notes
notes.unit: Text models are billed per million tokens, with separate prices for input, output and cache reads; image models are billed per image or per million output tokens.
notes.estimate: Per-image prices marked with ≈ are estimated at 1024×1024 (about {tokens} output tokens); actual cost varies with size and quality.
notes.longContext: When the input of a single request exceeds the context threshold of a model, the whole request is billed at the long-context price.
notes.edit: Image-to-image and inpainting also count the tokens of the input image, usually a small share of the total.
notes.currency: CNY prices are converted at $1 = ¥{rate} for reference only; wallets are always charged in USD.
notes.editions: Prices on this page are what the selected channel is billed; the Enterprise channel is priced by contract. See how the channels differ on the <link>channels page</link>.

items.q1: Is the price on this page what I actually pay?
items.a1: Yes. The displayed price is what the selected channel is billed, and every charge is itemized in the console.
items.q2: Why do prices differ across channels?
items.a2: Channels come with different capacity quality and availability targets: Shared runs on capacity shared by many users, Dedicated on premium capacity with priority scheduling, and Enterprise is set up for a single company with an availability agreement.
items.q3: Are there subscription fees or minimum spend?
items.a3: No. Usage is deducted from your balance as it happens; there is no monthly fee.
items.q4: Am I charged for failed image requests?
items.a4: Requests that fail upstream are not billed. Successful generations are billed per image or per token.
items.a5: The Dedicated and Enterprise channels support bank transfer and VAT invoices.
items.a6: They are converted at the fixed rate noted on the page, for reference only. Billing is in USD.

custom.title: Enterprise channel pricing is set by contract
custom.desc: Capacity set up for you and an availability agreement, quoted on your usage.
